about.title: Santee Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall accidents happen quietly — a wet floor near a Town Center storefront, a cracked walkway outside an apartment off N Magnolia Avenue, poor lighting in a parking structure near SR-52. What follows is rarely quiet: an ER visit, missed work, and questions about who's responsible. Under California law, a property owner or manager can be held liable if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors. Proving that notice is often the hardest part of a Santee premises case, which is why documenting the scene and locking down surveillance footage early matters so much. We handle premises liability cases — we can evaluate what happened, gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options. There's no charge for a case review, and no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Santee Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Crux of the Case
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. We can help identify inspection records, maintenance logs, or prior complaints that establish that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Santee businesses recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation letters can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you're partly at fault, though your share of fault reduces your compensation. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Santee?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. That window shrinks significantly if the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city facility or park, so it's worth having a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the fall happened on Mission Gorge Road or near SR-52 on a busy shopping day?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors like Mission Gorge Road see heavier foot traffic, which can mean more spills, debris, or worn flooring going unaddressed. We can look into whether the business had a pattern of complaints or inadequate maintenance schedules for that location.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront for a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we typically work on a contingency basis, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a settlement or award.
